sourceAnchors.visualArbitrationNote: Printed page 486 visually resolves section V, `Spezifischer Faktorenverband der Konversionshysterie`, as a four-factor association: k−; p± or 0 with positive variant noted in parentheses; e+ with 0 variant noted in parentheses; hy+ with 0 variant noted in parentheses. Canonical OCR severely damages the heading and formula row, so the admitted PDF governs the factor signs and parenthetical variants.

romanianRendering: În rezumatul experimental al Konversionshysterie, Szondi dă un Faktorenverband specific cu patru factori: k−; p±/0(+) ; e+(0) ; hy+(0). Variantele din paranteze sunt păstrate ca atare, nu simplificate într-un singur profil obligatoriu.
doctrinalStatement: `Spezifischer Faktorenverband der Konversionshysterie` este prezentat pe p. 486 ca o asociere de patru factori, vizual: `k−`, `p±/0(+)`, `e+(0)`, `hy+(0)`. Nucleul este păstrat ca schemă source-defined cu variante explicite, nu ca un profil unic și nu ca diagnostic autonom. Prezența izolată a unuia sau a două semne nu satisface nici măcar structura acestui Faktorenverband și trebuie citită în contextul mecanismului paroxysmal + Ich-Abwehr deja reprezentat.
conditions: Use the four-factor association as printed, preserving parenthetical variants rather than normalizing them away.
Interpret only together with the source's Konversionshysterie mechanism and general multi-factor syndrome criteria.
exceptions: Do not infer Konversionshysterie from k−, p, e or hy alone.
Do not collapse the parenthetical alternatives into one mandatory reaction for every case.
Do not convert the historical syndrome core into a contemporary diagnosis.
scopeNotes: The many Triebklasse and Triebformel variants immediately above this section remain source-atlas material rather than separate doctrine objects.
The four-factor core is retained because it is explicitly labelled `Spezifischer Faktorenverband`, unlike the surrounding case-like variants.

relations.note: Adds the source's compact four-factor syndrome association to the already represented paroxysmal + partial-Entfremdung mechanism.
Provides one source-defined four-factor association within the general multi-factor syndrome framework.
